title: Accelerated Trust Path: tokenized evidence exchange & dynamic insurance offsets
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Pilot a token-based evidence exchange that speeds vendor onboarding by automatically mapping vendor artifacts to risk tiers and applying insurance offsets to onboarding fees.
description:
Background: Procurement cycle times and manual SOC2 evidence collection are a major blocker for enterprise deals. Current onboarding requires repeated email exchange and manual verification by Legal and Security, which increases time-to-contract and adds friction for small vendors with partial attestations.

Proposal: Build an 'Accelerated Trust Path' that lets vendors upload verifiable artifacts (signed attestations, SOC2 excerpts, insurance certificates) into the vendor portal. Each artifact is normalized into a lightweight token (JSON-LD verifiable credential) that maps to a set of controls and a risk score. The platform will: (1) automatically validate token signatures and insurance policy fields via partner API, (2) compute a temporary risk tier, (3) offer a calculated onboarding credit / insurance-offset to reduce procurement review steps, and (4) surface a single summary card for Legal/Security with links to raw evidence.

Why unique: Instead of a static SOC2 bundle, this creates a machine-readable, auditable evidence layer that reduces manual review and enables conditional economic incentives (insurance offsets) for vendors who maintain verifiable coverage and controls.

Scope for pilot: 3 vendors (two small ISVs, one channel partner) using the Redwood vendor portal alpha. Integrations: insurance validation API (InsureAPI), signed-credential library (vc-js), and a simple mapping service that translates tokens to Redwood's risk taxonomy. The pilot excludes full legal contract automation — Legal will still approve final contracts but should be able to fast-track reviews when tokens meet pass thresholds.

Success metrics: reduce median onboarding time from initial intake to contract signature by >= 40% for pilot vendors; reduce manual evidence pulls by SRE/Security by >= 60%; demonstrate accurate insurance parse rate >= 95% on sampled policies.
acceptance_criteria: Vendor portal accepts signed evidence tokens (PDF with embedded JSON-LD or standalone VC) and stores a verifiable artifact record.
Automated signature and schema validation runs on upload and flags mismatches with human-readable errors.
Insurance API integration returns policy validity and key fields (carrier, policy number, effective/expiry) for >= 95% of pilot uploads.
System computes a risk tier score and displays a single onboarding summary card for Legal/Security with one-click 'Fast-Track' recommendation when thresholds met.
Pilot demonstrates >= 40% reduction in median time-to-contract and >= 60% reduction in manual evidence handling for the pilot cohort.
All pilot artifacts are stored with immutability metadata and an audit trail suitable for later compliance review.
Legal approves the pilot playbook and a sample contract clause for 'insurance offset' language documented in a Confluence page.
Rollout plan documented (alpha -> beta -> enterprise) with clear rollback criteria if false positives in validation exceed 10%.
notes: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with Procurement, Security, Legal, and Engineering. Agreed to 3-vendor pilot and to treat tokens as advisory (Legal retains final sign-off).
2025-02-19: Engineering spike completed on vc-js; prototype can verify sample JSON-LD credentials. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rwd-onboarding/pull/412
2025-02-25: Legal draft of insurance-offset clause in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PROC/pages/Accelerated+Trust+Path+Insurance+Offsets
2025-02-28: Procurement identified InsureAPI as preferred partner for policy parsing; engineering to scope integration (Auth: OAuth2, rate limits 1200/mo for pilot).
2025-03-02: UX mockups for portal upload flow and summary card added to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/XYZ/accelerated-trust-path

2025-03-04: Security reviewed initial threat model; decided to store only artifact hashes and signed tokens in Redwood DB, raw PDFs stored encrypted in S3 with KMS. Action: ENG-3124 for S3 lifecycle and KMS policy changes.
Next steps: engineering to deliver basic upload+validation MVP (sprint 2025-W10), run pilot onboarding workshops with 3 vendors, capture time-to-contract baseline metrics before and after.
